Predicted by hand from the archived text before recording (BUG-0094): wages $4,000; a business with receipts $5,000 and office expense $15,000, Schedule C line 31 a loss of $10,000 (all investment at risk); Schedule 1 line 3 and line 10 -$10,000; no self-employment tax on a loss; adjusted gross income $4,000 - $10,000 = -$6,000. No medical expenses (Schedule A line 1 $0). Line 2 enters line 11b at no less than zero (amb.2025.sa_medical_negative_agi), so line 3 is $0, line 4 is $0 and line 17 is $0; the signed reading would give line 3 -$450 and line 4 $450.

Predicted by hand from the archived text before recording (BUG-0094): the same return as audit.sa.negative_agi_medical with $1,000 of medical and dental expenses on Schedule A line 1; adjusted gross income -$6,000. Line 2 $0, line 3 $0, line 4 $1,000 - $0 = $1,000 (the whole of line 1, never more), line 17 $1,000 (no other itemized deductions); the signed reading would give line 4 $1,450.

Stage 13, predicted by hand from the archived instructions before recording: married filing separately (refused overall at Schedule 3 line 11; Schedule A still figured): state and local income tax $30,000; AGI $100,000 below the $250,000 threshold for a separate return, so the $40,000 ceiling is not reduced; half for a separate return, $20,000; line 5e the smaller of $30,000 and $20,000, $20,000.

Stage 13, predicted by hand from the archived instructions before recording: as above with AGI $400,000: $150,000 over the $250,000 threshold, reduced by 30% = $45,000, the ceiling $40,000 - $45,000 is below the $10,000 floor, so $10,000; half, $5,000; line 5e $5,000.

Stage 16, predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi (Schedule 1 line 8, Schedule A, the Tax Table, the EIC), i1040sca, i1040s8812 and p525, by two independent agents that did not see the encoding and agreed on every shared value; recorded after comparison. Facts: Single. Wages $60,000. Gambling winnings $5,000 (Form W-2G box 1); gambling losses $7,000. State income tax paid $4,000; home mortgage interest (Form 1098) $9,000. Working (predictor A): s1 8b gambling winnings 5,000 (i1040gi Line 8b p.90); s1 9 = 5,000; s1 10 = 5,000 -> f1040 line 8. f1040 1z 60,000; 9 = 65,000; 10 = 0; 11a/11b AGI 65,000. Sch A: 5a 4,000; 5d 4,000; 5e smaller of 5d or 40,000 = 4,000 (AGI under 500,000; f1040sa line 5e); 7 = 4,000; 8a 9,000; 8e 9,000; 10 9,000; 16 gambling losses only to the extent of winnings on s1 8b (i1040sca line 16): min(7,000, 5,000) = 5,000; 17 = 4,000+9,000+5,000 = 18,000 > standard 15,750 (single, i1040gi Standard Deduction) so itemize: 12e = 18,000; 14 = 18,000; 15 = 65,000 - 18,000 = 47,000; 16 Tax Table single 47,000-47,050 = 5,405; 18 = 5,405 (no Schedule 2).

BUG-0084. Joint return, wages $60,000 and $50,000; the spouse was born in 1960, has no SSN valid for employment and died in 2025 before reaching 65. i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, Death of spouse in 2025, "don't check the box that says 'Spouse was born before January 2, 1961'"; p501 p. 23: no age box, so the MFJ base $31,500 (line 12e), line 15 $78,500 and Tax Table tax $8,946 (line 16, the $78,500 to $78,550 row, married filing jointly).
